stories.title: Inventory sheet for the food bank
stories.body: I volunteer at a neighbourhood food bank on Saturdays. Stock was tracked on paper and we kept running out of tinned goods. I wrote a short Python script that reads the weekly donations spreadsheet and prints what to ask for. We stopped running out within a month.

stories.title: Explaining the new rota to eleven volunteers
stories.body: After ten years as a nurse I was the only one at the food bank who could explain things calmly to people who were anxious about computers. I ran two short sessions on the new sign-up tool and wrote a one-page guide with screenshots. Nobody dropped out over it.

stories.title: Getting the wholesaler to deliver on time
stories.body: Our wholesaler delivered late three weeks in a row. I phoned their dispatcher, learned their cut-off time, and moved our order to fit it. Deliveries have been on time since.

stories.title: Smart meter that reset itself
stories.body: At an electronics plant abroad I handled returns of smart meters that rebooted at random. I traced the resets to a brownout on one supply rail, wrote a Python script to scan the test logs for the same signature across 4,000 units, and the design team changed the capacitor.

stories.title: Teaching the line operators a new dashboard
stories.body: When we replaced paper test sheets with a dashboard, the operators distrusted it. I sat on the line for a week, explained each number in plain words, and let them correct me. Adoption went from half the shifts to all of them.

stories.title: Sensor batch that failed incoming checks
stories.body: A sensor supplier shipped a batch outside tolerance. I documented the failures with measurements, called their quality contact, and agreed a replacement batch plus a tighter incoming check. The line was stopped for one day instead of two weeks.

stories.title: Ordering script for my uncle's restaurant
stories.body: I never finished school but I taught myself Python from library books. I wrote a script that turns the kitchen's daily sales into a supplier order list. The restaurant now wastes less fresh produce.

stories.title: Showing the cook how the till reports work
stories.body: The cook did not trust the till reports. I walked through one day's numbers on a napkin, explained where each figure came from, and showed which ones to ignore. He now reads the report himself every morning.

stories.title: Running my father's care for two years
stories.body: I left work to care for my father after his stroke. I coordinated three siblings, a home nurse and the municipality, kept everyone informed with a weekly message, and stayed steady through hard nights.

stories.title: The care diary
stories.body: I kept a daily diary of medication, meals and mood so that any relative or nurse could take over without a phone call. The home nurse started using the same format for her own visits.

stories.title: Radios that came back with the same fault
stories.body: My family runs a small electronics repair shop. A batch of handheld radios kept coming back with weak audio. I compared the failures, found they all had a cracked solder joint near the jack, and changed how we reflow it. The repeat returns stopped.

stories.title: Disagreement with a parts wholesaler
stories.body: A wholesaler sent us the wrong connectors twice and refused a refund. I gathered the order emails and photos and wrote to their manager. They credited the order.

stories.title: Ticket readers that froze after an update
stories.body: At a bus depot (fictional) I do IT support for the drivers. After an overnight update the ticket readers froze on about one bus in five, mostly in the cold early morning. I kept a log of every freeze, traced a fault to a firmware timing issue between the reader and the payment module, and got the supplier to fix it. The patched firmware went out the next week.

stories.title: Teaching drivers the new handheld
stories.body: When the depot got new handheld terminals, drivers were afraid of breaking them. I made a laminated card with four steps and ran short sessions between shifts. Support calls about the terminals dropped within two weeks.

stories.title: Shift swap sheet
stories.body: Shift swaps were agreed by phone and often lost. I built a shared sheet with a few formulas so that a swap shows as covered or not at a glance. The dispatcher uses it daily.

stories.title: Power cut in the district
stories.body: I was a student when the power failed across my district for two days. I volunteered with the local engineers, helped find that a transformer fuse had tripped because of an overloaded feeder, and held the safety line while the crew worked.

stories.title: Coordinating the repair crews
stories.body: I carried messages between the municipal crew and a private contractor who did not share a language. I wrote the steps in both languages so nobody had to guess, and the work finished a day early.

stories.title: Field radios that lost range
stories.body: During my service I was the technician for a unit's field radios. I found that a batch lost range because of corroded antenna connectors, replaced them, and wrote a short checklist so the next crew would check them first.

stories.title: Briefing recruits on the new equipment
stories.body: I explained the new radio kit to new recruits who had never used one, using plain words and a live demonstration. Every recruit passed the practical test on the first try.

stories.title: Spare parts from the central depot
stories.body: Spare parts from the central depot were slow. I phoned their planner, learned their ordering cycle and moved our requests to fit it. Wait time fell from three weeks to one.
